assignments.reason: Tikkun for pgam habrit (repair of the covenant blemish) shares the essential nature of Package 1: the brit (covenant) IS the derech/isha nexus in its holy form. The pgam habrit is defined in this Torah as the corruption of the derech — 'ki hishchit kol basar et darko' — and its tikkun is the restoration of that same path-channel. The tikkun belongs to the derech/isha structural domain by essential nature. Polarity is good because it is the corrective, holy restoration of the covenant.

Tikkun habrit (repairing the covenant) is essentially the same concept as 'tikkun l'pgam habrit' — the restoration of the brit, which is the holy form of the derech/isha nexus. The covenant (brit) is structurally identical to the path/woman channel: it IS the proper, holy configuration of derech and isha. This shares the essential nature of Package 1. Polarity is good because it is the act of holy restoration.

assignments.node_text: מוצא זווגו, והיא אינה כנגדו, רק כרצונו
assignments.reason: Finding one's match, with her aligned to his will, is the fully realized holy form of the isha/derech nexus. The zivug (match) IS the isha (woman) of Package 1 in her proper, holy orientation — she is no longer 'k'negdo' (opposing) but 'kir'tzono' (according to his will). This is the isha/derech relationship functioning correctly. By essential nature this belongs to the woman/path domain. Polarity is good because this is the positive, holy outcome of the tikkun.

The desire returning toward him ('naaseh bah ratzon eilav') describes the isha's will being restored — she turns back toward him. This is about the woman (isha) and her orientation within the relational channel (derech). By essential nature this is the isha of Package 1 in her corrected state: her ratzon (will) realigned with the holy direction of the path. Polarity is good because this is the positive restoration of the woman's desire toward the holy union.

unassigned_nodes.reason: The kavvanot (mystical intentions) of Elul are a spiritual practice — an active, holy mechanism whose secret is 'haNotein bayam derech' (giving a path in the sea). They do not share the essential bechina-nature of either existing package. They are not themselves the path/woman channel (Package 1), nor are they the sea/faith receptive domain (Package 2). They are the agent that illuminates the derech INTO the yam — bridging both packages causally but belonging to neither by essential nature. Their nature is that of a spiritual remedy/practice, which is a distinct conceptual domain not captured by the existing bechina-based packages.

This is the same essential concept as 'kavvanot Elul' (the kavvanot of Elul as the tikkun for this matter). It describes the Elul kavvanot in their role as the corrective remedy. Like the node above, it is an active spiritual practice that bridges both packages causally (it illuminates derech in yam) but does not share the bechina-nature of either package. It is neither the path/woman structure nor the sea/faith domain — it is the holy practice that connects them.
